pr.title: Phase 1b: add alias and distribution list administration
pr.body:
The web panel can now manage domain aliases, distribution lists, posting settings and list members through explicit native commands and REST endpoints. It adds searchable, paginated lists, activation controls, member editing and deletion, and confirmation for consequential posting-policy changes.

Server administrators can manage every domain; domain administrators can manage only their own. The native dispatcher checks domain/list/object ownership, validates single addresses and allowed fields before persistence, rejects duplicate members and direct self-targets, and uses existing quota/collision rules and cache invalidation. New aliases and lists default disabled; lists default members-only with SMTP authentication required. No database schema, web SQL or COM backend dependency is added.

Posting modes preserve the existing engine's envelope-sender semantics. Required SMTP authentication does not bind the envelope sender to the authenticated identity; the UI and REST contract explain this, including the domain-sender mode's treatment of nonexistent mailboxes. Public posting and authentication settings remain explicit administrator choices.

Validation for head `3e83eaddfd2f23daf7255ae17bf22a67e3bc8b70`:
- Native Release and .NET builds passed; development-host compilation only.
- Disposable Hyper-V VM: 26 DNS + 132 HTTP/security + 2 HTTPS + 152 native assertions passed (312 total), plus 2 separate pipe identity assertions.
- Native tests include real SMTP RCPT probes for alias activation/deletion, all four posting modes, required authentication and member-cache invalidation. They send no DATA, queue no messages and perform no external delivery.
- All 15 selected existing distribution-list/alias-name regression tests passed with zero failures or inconclusive results.
- VM browser fixtures passed alias/list/member CRUD, activation and deletion confirmations/cancellation, password/session regression workflows and mobile layout checks.
- The control-character validation regression was reproduced in the VM before its fix. Original VM server/database/configuration and the temporary checkpoint were restored.
- CI passed: Release x64, GCC, Clang, all four installed-server database jobs and installer publication. Each backend passed all 312 management assertions and the expanded browser workflows.
- NUnit: 1,315 tests per backend. Compact/PostgreSQL/MySQL: 1,205 passed, 0 failed, 0 warnings, 34 inconclusive, 76 skipped. Express: 1,206 passed, 0 failed, 0 warnings, 34 inconclusive, 75 skipped. Totals match the previous baseline.

Updates the API contract, CI inventory, README, roadmap, requirements and shared agent handoff, including merged PR #35 and this authorized next slice. Renaming alias/list addresses, bulk membership operations, complete graph-cycle validation, indexed database pagination and the rest of Phase 1b remain separate work.

Pause for maintainer review after this PR; do not start the next task or merge without explicit instruction.

+Aliases, lists and members use the same `search`/`offset`/`limit` contract. Server administrators
+can manage every domain; domain administrators can manage only their own; ordinary mailbox
+users cannot use these operations. Parent IDs come from routes, never from writable fields.
+Foreign-domain requests are denied and mismatched object/list IDs return 404.
+
+Alias POST requires `address` and `target`; `active` is optional and defaults to false. PATCH
+accepts `target` and/or `active`. The source address must belong to the owning domain; the
+target can be local or external. Domain/address duplicate checks and configured alias limits
+use existing native persistence. Direct self-forwarding is rejected. Renaming is not exposed.
+
+List POST requires `address`; optional fields are `active` (default false), `mode` (default 1),
+`requireAuth` (default true) and `requireAddress` (default empty). PATCH accepts those fields
+except `address`. Existing domain list limits and account/alias/list collisions remain enforced.
+
+| Mode | Meaning |
+|---|---|

commit.message:
Add native alias and distribution list administration

Expose domain-scoped alias, list and member CRUD through REST and the responsive panel. Preserve native posting semantics, use conservative creation defaults, validate addresses before persistence and cover parent permissions and SMTP cache invalidation. Update the roadmap, API contract and shared project memory.

issue.body:
Adds the agreed message-identifier and IMAP UID lifecycle plan to the engineering roadmap. The plan separates stable internal IDs from standard 32-bit IMAP identities and defines staged delivery for boundary fixes, transactional per-folder allocation, controlled UIDVALIDITY renewal, recovery and operator controls.

Acceptance covers signed/unsigned boundaries, exact API IDs, concurrency and notification ordering, stale-session fencing, crashes and backup/restore, client resynchronization, POP3 UIDLs, all supported databases and future SQLite. It explicitly avoids promises of unlimited per-folder capacity or invisible resync, and tracks correction/publication of the outdated database-maintenance page.

Refreshes README, roadmap, CI inventory and agent handoff to reflect merged PRs #36/#37 and the verified 312 management assertions per database at #36. Records the maintainer's deferred end-of-modernization CodeQL re-audit. The next proposed Phase 1b slice is mailbox forwarding and automatic replies, followed by remaining advanced administration, queue/rules/routes/listeners, DNS/DKIM lifecycle, SpamAssassin packaging, certificate management, Defender, hosting and PHP retirement.

This is documentation only. It starts no UID or administration implementation and makes no website or alert-state changes. Each implementation PR still requires separate maintainer confirmation.

Validation: all 70 local Markdown links in the edited documents resolved; git diff --check passed. No product runtime tests were run on the development host. CI passed on commit 6c39f8fe52692158fa99da78a417230e42eb2a20: Release x64, all four database regression/management jobs (Compact, MySQL, PostgreSQL and SQL Server Express), installer publication, CodeQL and gcc/clang portable-core checks.
